questions.text:
Consider an Entity-Relationship (ER) model in which entity sets E1 and E2 are connected by an m : n relationship R12. E1 and E3 are connected by a 1 : n (1 on the side of E1 and n on the side of E3) relationship R13.

E1 has two single-valued attributes a11 and a12 of which a11 is the key attribute. E2 has two single-valued attributes a21 and a22 of which a21 is the key attribute. E3 has two single-valued attributes a31 and a32 of which a31 is the key attribute. The relationships do not have any attributes.

If a relational model is derived from the above ER model, then the minimum number of relations that would be generated if all the relations are in 3NF is _______.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- E1(a11, a12), E2(a21, a22): one relation each
- R12 is m:n: needs its own relation (a11, a21)
- R13 is 1:n: add a11 as a foreign key in E3(a31, a32, a11), no separate table

Total = 4

Answer: 4

questions.text: A file is organized so that the ordering of data records is the same as or close to the ordering of data entries in some index. Then that index is called
questions.solution:
When the data file is stored in (nearly) the same order as the index entries, the index is called clustered.

Answer: Clustered

questions.solution:

Answer: the projection operation, except that SELECT in SQL retains duplicates

questions.text: Consider a system where each file is associated with a 16 bit number. For each file, each user should have the read and write capability. How much memory is needed to store each user's access data?
questions.solution:
16-bit file numbers [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]2^{16}[/latex] files. Each needs 2 bits (read, write) per user.

[latex]2^{16}\times2=2^{17}[/latex] bits = [latex]2^{14}[/latex] bytes = 16 KB

Answer: 16 KB
